title: Open/Add Specific Colorways
description:
The new update to our Colorway Editor in CLO 2025.1 allows you to choose specific colorways to import when opening or adding garment files.

Check out other new features here:https://clo3d.com/en/clo/features

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord?utm_campaign=multi_item_banner_JointheOfficialCLODiscord&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=later-linkinbio

summary: ```markdown # Open/Add Specific Colorways ## Introduction Hey everyone, it's Phoebe here, and I have some great updates to share with you for Colorways. So let's dive on in and have some fun while we learn. ## Adding a Cover-Up Alright, so here I have a bathing suit, but I definitely want to bring in a cover for it. Now, first, what I just want to show you all is if I go to **Production**, then **Colorway**. ### Viewing Colorways Okay, what you can see here in my Production and Colorway is that I've got four different colorways. Now, I'm going to bring in a cover, so I'm going to go to **File**, then **Add Garment**. Here’s my cover-up, and I'm going to add this in. ## Choosing Colorways Now, when I go back to **Production** and **Colorway**, I'm going to bring in a cover for it. So, when I add this in, I'll then have an option for colorways. I can choose **All**, **Custom**, and I can pick them. I'm going to do **Custom** and select which colorways I want. I also have four colorways here, so I’m going to just hit **OK** and bring in all four colorways. ### Confirmation of Colorways I'll hit **Alright** and then **OK**. Great! Now I have all these colorways. They look fantastic. I can go into **Colorway 2**. ## Editing Buttons What’s really nice here is for my buttons; I can start to edit them. I can simply go to this drop-down, this little drop icon, and see more options. I could just click here and go straight into the color and change this color out. ### Applying Color Changes Maybe I want it to be more here. I’ll hit **Apply**. Then I can select this one and **Apply** again. I can then go to another color. Oh! What I first want to do is make sure... I need to ensure these aren't linked. That was on me. ### Managing Links These were all linked, which is why all of the colors were changing. So, I just needed to change that quickly and easily. Now, I can go through with these buttons, select them, and start changing the colors around. Cool! Easy. ## Saving Higher Quality Images That’s a really nice update we have here. I also can go into **Save Image**, and now I can even choose, like, **Colorway Editor**. I can specify that I want this 4x, so I want it four times larger, and I want this to be really big. ### Finalizing the Image Then I'm going to hit **OK**, and it’s going to be a higher-quality image for my colorways. This way, I can see all of them a little bit easier without worrying about rendering each one out. ## Adding More Colorways To just show you also another option, let’s say I want to add in another colorway here. Let’s add in two more. For these two additional colorways, I'm going to keep the bathing suit as it is, but I’m going to select this cover-up and delete it. ### Updating Colorways Now, I have six colorways—an increase in options. If I go to **File**, then **Add Garment** for the cover-up again, I can still select all colorways. However, remember that I only have four colorways. ### Understanding Colorway Addition You might wonder what’s going to happen. What happens is that the first colorway is then going to be added to the extra ones, so I’m going to hit **OK**. You can see here that the first colorway is added to five and six, the extra two that I added. ## Conclusion Thanks so much for watching! If you have any questions, use that comment section down below. Don't forget to like and subscribe. There are so many great videos for you to learn and to help you in your CLO journey. Keep having fun in CLO. Thanks again! ```
